subject: B
topic: All topics of GK & Current Affairs India (mixed)

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Non-Cooperation Movement was launched by Mahatma Gandhi in the year:
questions.explanation: Gandhi launched the Non-Cooperation Movement in August 1920, calling for boycotts of British institutions. 1922 saw its withdrawal after Chauri Chaura, 1930 was the Salt Satyagraha, and 1942 was the Quit India Movement, so only 1920 marks its launch.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Constitution:

(i) The Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950.
(ii) The Constituent Assembly was chaired by Dr. Rajendra Prasad.
(iii) B.R. Ambedkar was the chairman of the Drafting Committee.
(iv) The Indian Constitution has no amendments.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Constitution came into force on 26 January 1950, Rajendra Prasad chaired the Constituent Assembly, and Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are true. Statement (iv) is false because the Constitution has been amended many times, so any option including (iv) is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The largest state in India by population is:
questions.explanation: Uttar Pradesh is the most populous state in India. Bihar and Maharashtra are large but less populous than UP, and Madhya Pradesh is smaller in population than all three, so only Uttar Pradesh is the largest by population.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following authors with their books:

Column I:
(a) Kalidasa
(b) Chanakya
(c) Panini
(d) Kalhana

Column II:
(i) Ashtadhyayi
(ii) Rajatarangini
(iii) Arthashastra
(iv) Abhijnanashakuntalam

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Kalidasa wrote 'Abhijnanashakuntalam', Chanakya wrote 'Arthashastra', Panini wrote 'Ashtadhyayi', and Kalhana wrote 'Rajatarangini', giving (a)-(iv), (b)-(iii), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii). The other options swap Kalidasa with Chanakya or misplace Panini, which are historically incorrect.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Digital India' programme was launched in the year:
questions.explanation: The Digital India programme was launched by the Government of India on 1 July 2015 to enhance digital infrastructure and delivery of services. 2010 and 2014 predate its launch, and 2018 is after, so only 2015 is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are traditional folk dances of India?

(i) Bihu
(ii) Bhangra
(iii) Ballet
(iv) Garba

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Bihu (Assam), Bhangra (Punjab) and Garba (Gujarat) are all traditional Indian folk dances, so (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct. Ballet is a Western classical dance form originating in Europe and is not an Indian folk dance, so any option that includes ballet is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Iron Man of India' is:
questions.explanation: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel is known as the Iron Man of India for uniting the princely states after independence. Nehru was India's first PM, and Bhagat Singh and Bose were freedom fighters with their own titles, so only Patel earns the 'Iron Man' epithet.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India is a member of the G20.
Reason (R): The G20 is a forum of the world's major economies.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Both statements are true: India is a G20 member, and the G20 is a forum of the world's major economies. India, being one of the largest world economies, is exactly why it is a member of the G20, so (R) correctly explains (A). Other options fail because both statements are true and (R) does explain (A).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The __________ is the highest peacetime gallantry award of India.
questions.explanation: The Ashok Chakra is India's highest peacetime gallantry award. The Param Vir Chakra is the highest wartime gallantry award, the Kirti Chakra is a peacetime award ranking below the Ashok Chakra, and the Vir Chakra is a wartime decoration ranking below the PVC, so only the Ashok Chakra is the highest peacetime honour.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following table shows India's rice production (in million tonnes):

2019 — 118
2020 — 122
2021 — 130
2022 — 132

In which year was rice production the highest?
questions.explanation: In 2022 production was 132 million tonnes, the highest of the four years, ahead of 130 in 2021, 122 in 2020 and 118 in 2019. 2021 is the second highest, not the peak, so 2022 is the correct year for the maximum rice production.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Who is the head of the Union Council of Ministers in India?
questions.explanation: The Prime Minister heads the Union Council of Ministers and is the leader of the executive at the Centre. The President is the constitutional head of state, the Chief Justice heads the judiciary, and the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha presides over that house, so the PM is correct for the Council of Ministers.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the President of India:

(i) The President is the head of state.
(ii) The President is directly elected by the people of India.
(iii) The President's term of office is five years.
(iv) The President is a part of Parliament.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The President is head of state, has a five-year term, and is part of Parliament, so (i), (iii) and (iv) are true. Statement (ii) is false because the President is elected indirectly by an electoral college (elected legislators), not directly by the people, so any option including (ii) is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The National Anthem of India is set to music composed originally on the tune of:
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore composed both the words and the tune of 'Jana Gana Mana'. Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay wrote 'Vande Mataram', Iqbal wrote 'Saare Jahan Se Achha', and Kavi Pradeep composed 'Ae Mere Watan Ke Logon', so none of them wrote the Anthem's tune; Tagore is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following classical dances with their states:

Column I:
(a) Bharatanatyam
(b) Kathakali
(c) Kuchipudi
(d) Manipuri

Column II:
(i) Andhra Pradesh
(ii) Manipur
(iii) Tamil Nadu
(iv) Kerala

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Bharatanatyam is from Tamil Nadu, Kathakali from Kerala, Kuchipudi from Andhra Pradesh, and Manipuri from Manipur, giving (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(i), (d)-(ii). The other options swap Tamil Nadu with Kerala or misplace Manipur, which do not match each classical dance's home state.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Nationalist Movement' newspaper 'Kesari' was published by:
questions.explanation: Bal Gangadhar Tilak founded and published 'Kesari' (in Marathi) as a nationalist newspaper. Gandhi published 'Young India' and 'Harijan', Lala Lajpat Rai edited 'The People', and Bipin Chandra Pal wrote for other publications, so none of them ran Kesari; Tilak is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India?

(i) Ellora Caves
(ii) Sun Temple of Konark
(iii) India Gate
(iv) Elephanta Caves

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Ellora Caves, the Sun Temple of Konark and Elephanta Caves are all UNESCO World Heritage Sites in India, so (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct. India Gate is a war memorial in Delhi and is not listed as a UNESCO Heritage Site, so any option including India Gate is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Reserve Bank of India was nationalised in the year:
questions.explanation: The RBI was nationalised on 1 January 1949 under the Reserve Bank (Transfer to Public Ownership) Act, 1948. 1947 was Independence, 1951 saw the First Five-Year Plan, and 1955 was the year the Imperial Bank became SBI, so only 1949 marks the RBI nationalisation.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Preamble is called the soul of the Constitution.
Reason (R): The Preamble sets out the ideals and objectives of the Constitution.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Both statements are true: the Preamble is famously called the soul of the Constitution, and it lays out the ideals and objectives of the document. Because it captures the core values, calling it the soul is precisely explained by its statement of ideals, so (R) correctly explains (A). Other options fail because both statements are true and (R) does explain (A).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Delhi Sultanate' era in India began after the:
questions.explanation: Muhammad Ghori's victory over Prithviraj Chauhan at the Second Battle of Tarain in 1192 paved the way for the Delhi Sultanate, established formally in 1206. The First Battle of Panipat (1526) began the Mughal empire, and Plassey (1757) and Buxar (1764) marked British ascendancy, so Tarain 1192 is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Indian rupee coin is minted by the Government of India through the:
questions.explanation: Rupee coins are minted by the India Government Mints (under the Ministry of Finance/SPMCIL). The Reserve Bank of India issues currency notes (except one-rupee note) but not coins, and the Ministries of External Affairs and Home Affairs handle unrelated portfolios, so only the India Government Mint is correct for coin minting.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Armed Forces:

(i) The Indian Army is the largest of the three service branches.
(ii) The President is the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces.
(iii) The Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) is a position that heads all three services.
(iv) The Indian Air Force has no jet fighters.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Indian Army is the largest branch, the President is the Supreme Commander, and the CDS heads all three services, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are true. Statement (iv) is false because the IAF has many jet fighters such as the Su-30 MKI and Rafale, so any option including (iv) is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Poona Pact' between Mahatma Gandhi and B.R. Ambedkar was signed in the year:
questions.explanation: The Poona Pact was signed in September 1932 between Gandhi and Ambedkar to resolve the issue of separate electorates for the Depressed Classes. 1930 was the Salt Satyagraha, 1934 has no such pact, and 1935 saw the Government of India Act, so only 1932 fits.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The largest freshwater lake in India (by area) is often cited as:
questions.explanation: Wular Lake in Jammu & Kashmir is often cited as one of the largest freshwater lakes in India. Chilika Lake in Odisha is the largest brackish lake, not fresh water, the Dal Lake is much smaller, and Pushkar Lake is a small sacred lake, so among freshwater lakes Wular is the largest.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following states with their major festivals:

Column I:
(a) Kerala
(b) Assam
(c) Punjab
(d) Gujarat

Column II:
(i) Bihu
(ii) Baisakhi
(iii) Onam
(iv) Navaratri (Garba)

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Onam is celebrated in Kerala, Bihu in Assam, Baisakhi in Punjab, and Navaratri (Garba) in Gujarat, giving (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(ii), (d)-(iv). The other options swap Bihu with Onam or misplace Baisakhi, which do not match the states' principal festivals.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: 'Chandrayaan-3', which successfully soft-landed on the Moon, was a mission of:
questions.explanation: Chandrayaan-3, launched in 2023, was an Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) mission that soft-landed on the lunar south pole region. NASA is the American space agency, ESA is European, and CNSA is the Chinese national space administration, so only ISRO carried out Chandrayaan-3.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are Fundamental Rights under the Indian Constitution?

(i) Right to Equality
(ii) Right against Exploitation
(iii) Right to Property
(iv) Right to Constitutional Remedies

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Right to Equality, Right against Exploitation and Right to Constitutional Remedies are all Fundamental Rights, so (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct. The Right to Property was removed as a Fundamental Right by the 44th Amendment (1978) and is now only a legal right, so any option including (iii) is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Green Revolution' in India was chiefly associated with:
questions.explanation: The Green Revolution focused on boosting foodgrain (wheat and rice) production using high-yielding varieties. Milk is linked to the White Revolution, fisheries to the Blue Revolution, and cotton to the Fibre Revolution, so none of them is the Green Revolution focus; wheat and rice is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Supreme Court of India can review its own judgments.
Reason (R): The Supreme Court is the highest court of India.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Both statements are true: the Supreme Court can review its own judgments under Article 137, and it is the highest court of India. However, being the highest court does not by itself explain the review power (that comes from Article 137 specifically), so (R) does not correctly explain (A).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) guarantees at least __________ days of wage employment in a financial year.
questions.explanation: MGNREGA guarantees at least 100 days of wage employment per household in a financial year. 50, 75 and 125 days do not match the statutory number in the Act, so only 100 correctly fills the blank.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
The following table shows India's Olympic medals in four editions:

2008 — 3
2012 — 6
2016 — 2
2020 — 7

In which year did India win the most medals?
questions.explanation: India's 2020 Olympic medal count of 7 (Tokyo Olympics held in 2021) is the highest, ahead of 6 in 2012, 3 in 2008 and 2 in 2016. 2012 is the second highest, not the top, so 2020 is the correct year for the most medals.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Ashoka Chakra at the centre of the Indian flag has how many spokes?
questions.explanation: The Ashoka Chakra has 24 spokes, taken from the Lion Capital of Sarnath. Options 12, 20 and 36 do not match this well-established number of spokes on the flag's central wheel, so only 24 is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about India's climate:

(i) India experiences a monsoon-dominated climate.
(ii) The southwest monsoon typically arrives in Kerala first.
(iii) The northeast monsoon brings winter rain to Tamil Nadu.
(iv) India has no arid regions.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: India has a monsoon-dominated climate, the southwest monsoon arrives first in Kerala, and the northeast monsoon brings winter rain to Tamil Nadu, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are true. Statement (iv) is false because the Thar Desert makes north-west India an arid region, so any option including (iv) is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following:

Column I:
(a) Cricket
(b) Hockey
(c) Football
(d) Chess

Column II:
(i) Grandmaster
(ii) Century
(iii) Goal
(iv) Bully

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: A century belongs to cricket, a bully is a term in hockey, a goal is scored in football, and grandmaster is a chess title, giving (a)-(ii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(iii), (d)-(i). The other options swap century with goal or misplace grandmaster, which do not match each sport's terminology.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which is the state with the longest coastline in India?
questions.explanation: Gujarat has the longest coastline of any Indian state, about 1,600 km. Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu also have long coasts but shorter than Gujarat, and Kerala's coastline is around 590 km, so none of them exceeds Gujarat; Gujarat is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about Indian rivers:

(i) The Brahmaputra enters India through Arunachal Pradesh.
(ii) The Ganga is the longest river in India.
(iii) The Godavari is the longest river of peninsular India.
(iv) The Narmada flows into the Bay of Bengal.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Brahmaputra enters India through Arunachal Pradesh, the Ganga is India's longest river, and the Godavari is peninsular India's longest river, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are true. Statement (iv) is false because the Narmada flows westward into the Arabian Sea, not the Bay of Bengal, so any option including (iv) is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The unit of energy 'kilowatt-hour' is used to measure:
questions.explanation: The kilowatt-hour (kWh) measures electric energy consumption over time. Voltage is measured in volts, electric current in amperes, and electric power in watts (or kilowatts), so none of those uses kWh; electric energy is the correct quantity.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) is India's primary:
questions.explanation: The CBI is India's premier investigating agency handling major cases including corruption and organised crime. India's space agency is ISRO and health matters fall under the Health Ministry and bodies like ICMR, so those descriptions do not fit; 'investigating agency' is correct for the CBI.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Bhakra Nangal Dam is one of the largest dams in India.
Reason (R): It is built across the Sutlej river.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Both statements are true: the Bhakra Nangal Dam is among India's largest dams and is built across the Sutlej. However, the specific river it is on does not by itself explain its size (which depends on engineering scale), so (R) does not correctly explain (A). Other options fail because both statements are true.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Look East Policy' of India was initiated in the early:
questions.explanation: India's 'Look East Policy' was launched in the early 1990s under Prime Minister P.V. Narasimha Rao to strengthen ties with Southeast Asian nations. The 1970s and 1980s predate the policy, and the 2000s came after, so only the 1990s marks its initiation.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Panchayati Raj system:

(i) It was formally introduced by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment.
(ii) The 73rd Amendment was enacted in 1992.
(iii) It provides for a three-tier structure of local government in rural areas.
(iv) It applies only to urban areas.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The 73rd Amendment (1992) established a three-tier Panchayati Raj system for rural areas, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are true. Statement (iv) is false because Panchayati Raj is specifically for rural areas; the 74th Amendment covers urban local bodies, so any option including (iv) is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The Indian rupee is the legal tender in India.
Reason (R): The Reserve Bank of India controls monetary policy in India.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Both statements are true: the rupee is India's legal tender, and the RBI controls monetary policy. However, the RBI's monetary policy role is a broader central-banking function and does not by itself explain why the rupee is legal tender (that owes to statute), so (R) does not correctly explain (A).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are Ratna categories among the Padma awards?

(i) Padma Vibhushan
(ii) Padma Bhushan
(iii) Padma Shri
(iv) Padma Ratna

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: The Padma awards have three levels: Padma Vibhushan, Padma Bhushan and Padma Shri, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are correct. 'Padma Ratna' is not a recognised category among the Padma awards, so any option including it is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Kollam is a coastal city in which Indian state?
questions.explanation: Kollam is a coastal city in the state of Kerala. Karnataka has coastal cities like Mangalore, Tamil Nadu has Chennai, and Andhra Pradesh has Visakhapatnam, but none of them is called Kollam; Kollam belongs to Kerala.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'International Yoga Day' is observed every year on:
questions.explanation: The International Day of Yoga is observed on 21 June, adopted by the UN in 2014 on India's proposal. 5 September is Teachers' Day, 2 October is Gandhi Jayanti, and 14 November is Children's Day, so only 21 June corresponds to International Yoga Day.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The 'Mahatma Gandhi Setu' is a bridge across the __________ river.
questions.explanation: The Mahatma Gandhi Setu is a long road bridge across the Ganga near Patna, Bihar. The Yamuna, Godavari and Krishna rivers have their own bridges but not this one, so only the Ganga is the correct river spanned by the Mahatma Gandhi Setu.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about wildlife conservation in India:

(i) Project Tiger was launched in 1973.
(ii) The one-horned rhinoceros is a symbol of Kaziranga National Park.
(iii) The Asiatic lion is found in the Gir Forest of Gujarat.
(iv) India has no biosphere reserves.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Project Tiger began in 1973, Kaziranga is symbolised by the one-horned rhinoceros, and the Asiatic lion lives in Gir, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are true. Statement (iv) is false because India has several biosphere reserves such as the Nilgiri, Nanda Devi and Sundarbans, so any option including (iv) is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following personalities with their fields:

Column I:
(a) Amartya Sen
(b) Kailash Satyarthi
(c) Vikram Sarabhai
(d) Salim Ali

Column II:
(i) Ornithology
(ii) Space research
(iii) Economics
(iv) Children's rights

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Amartya Sen is an economist, Kailash Satyarthi is an activist for children's rights, Vikram Sarabhai led space research, and Salim Ali is famed for ornithology, giving (a)-(iii), (b)-(iv), (c)-(ii), (d)-(i). The other options swap economics with space or misplace children's rights, which are wrong pairings.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Right to Education (RTE) Act of India provides free and compulsory education for children in the age group of:
questions.explanation: The RTE Act, 2009 provides free and compulsory education for children aged 6 to 14 years. 3 to 6 is the pre-school age (covered separately), 6 to 18 goes beyond the Act's scope, and 14 to 18 is secondary schooling not covered by RTE's core mandate, so 6 to 14 is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The first Indian to win the Nobel Prize in Literature was:
questions.explanation: Rabindranath Tagore won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1913, the first Indian to do so. C.V. Raman won in Physics (1930), Amartya Sen in Economics (1998), and V.S. Naipaul in Literature (2001) but as a Trinidad-born British writer of Indian origin, so Tagore is the first Indian literature laureate.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Which is the highest waterfall in India?
questions.explanation: Kunchikal Falls in Karnataka, at about 455 m, is generally cited as India's highest waterfall. Jog Falls is famous but shorter (about 253 m), Hogenakkal is a series of small falls on the Kaveri, and Dudhsagar (Goa) is around 310 m tall, so Kunchikal is the tallest.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Constitution's Directive Principles:

(i) They are contained in Part IV of the Constitution.
(ii) They aim to establish a welfare state.
(iii) They are inspired by the Irish Constitution.
(iv) They are enforceable in a court of law.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: Directive Principles are in Part IV, aim at a welfare state, and were inspired by the Irish Constitution, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are true. Statement (iv) is false because the Directive Principles are non-justiciable and cannot be enforced by courts, so any option including (iv) is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Mansabdari System' was introduced by which Mughal Emperor?
questions.explanation: Akbar introduced the Mansabdari system to organise the civil and military administration of the Mughal Empire. Babur and Humayun preceded him and did not institute this system, and Aurangzeb continued it later, so only Akbar is credited with its introduction.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The 'Jallikattu' is a traditional sport primarily associated with:
questions.explanation: Jallikattu, a traditional bull-taming sport played during Pongal, is closely associated with Tamil Nadu. Kerala has other traditional sports, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh have their own local traditions, but Jallikattu belongs specifically to Tamil Nadu.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Match the following presidents with their tenure order:

Column I:
(a) Rajendra Prasad
(b) S. Radhakrishnan
(c) A.P.J. Abdul Kalam
(d) Pratibha Patil

Column II:
(i) Second President
(ii) First woman President
(iii) First President
(iv) 11th President (People's President)

Choose the correct match:
questions.explanation: Rajendra Prasad was the first President, S. Radhakrishnan the second, A.P.J. Abdul Kalam the 11th (People's President), and Pratibha Patil the first woman President, giving (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii). The other options swap first with second or misplace the first woman, which are historically wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The number of Union Territories in India as of 2024 is:
questions.explanation: After the 2019 and 2020 reorganisations (including the merger of Dadra & Nagar Haveli with Daman & Diu, and the creation of J&K and Ladakh UTs), India has 8 Union Territories. 7, 9 and 10 do not match this current count, so only 8 is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Which of the following are neighbouring countries that share a maritime border with India?

(i) Sri Lanka
(ii) Maldives
(iii) Uzbekistan
(iv) Indonesia

Select the correct combination:
questions.explanation: Sri Lanka lies across the Palk Strait, the Maldives are south-west in the Arabian Sea, and Indonesia lies south-east of the Andaman & Nicobar Islands, so all three share a maritime border with India and (i), (ii) and (iv) are correct. Uzbekistan is a landlocked Central Asian country, so any option including Uzbekistan is wrong.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) was established in the year:
questions.explanation: ISRO was established on 15 August 1969, superseding the earlier INCOSPAR (formed 1962). 1962 was the earlier committee, 1975 saw the launch of Aryabhata, and 1980 saw the SLV-3 launch, so only 1969 is the year of ISRO's formal establishment.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Given below are two statements, one labeled as Assertion (A) and the other as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): India is a federal state.
Reason (R): The Constitution of India divides powers between the Centre and the states through Union, State and Concurrent Lists.

Choose the correct option:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.correctAnswer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Both statements are true: India is a federal state, and the Constitution divides powers via the three lists. This division of powers is precisely what defines federalism, so (R) correctly explains (A). Other options fail because both statements are true and (R) does explain (A).

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText: Fill in the blank: The __________ is India's national aquatic animal.
questions.explanation: The Ganges River Dolphin was declared India's National Aquatic Animal in 2009. The peacock is the national bird, the Bengal Tiger is the national animal, and the Indian Elephant is the national heritage animal, so none of them is the aquatic animal; only the Ganges River Dolphin is correct.

questions.subject: B
questions.questionText:
Consider the following statements about the Indian Constitution's Preamble:

(i) It describes India as a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic.
(ii) It declares that we, the people of India, adopt the Constitution.
(iii) It was adopted with the Constitution on 26 November 1949.
(iv) The words 'socialist' and 'secular' were part of the original Preamble in 1949.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanation: The Preamble describes India as sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic, declares 'we, the people' adopting the Constitution, and was adopted on 26 November 1949, so (i), (ii) and (iii) are true. Statement (iv) is false because 'socialist' and 'secular' were added later by the 42nd Amendment (1976), so any option with (iv) is wrong.
